messages:
maya: Heads-up: following the last convo about Hosted->Private fallbacks, i've been sketching a tighter delegation model that pins tokens to artifact hashes so tokens can't be reused for other models. thoughts?

leo: Sounds promising. How would the binding look? token contains artifact_hash claim? single-use nonce?

maya: Exactly: token fields: aud=runtime, model_id, artifact_hash, nonce, exp. Sign with KMS. Runtime can prove it fetched an exact artifact before accepting inference ops.

ashley: That helps with theft scenarios. But it means token issuance must know artifact hash at request time. when do we compute that? at model publish time and store in registry.

leo: Right, canonical artifact manifest includes sha256. When a user pins model v2 -> we compute and persist artifact_hash. Token issuer references that.

ops: What about runtime-local cache warmups? If private runtime already has cached artifact (no fetch), we still want to verify token. Should token allow cache:read only for matching artifact hash?

maya: Token scope could include cache:(read|validate) and an optional field cached=true|false. If cached=true, issuer only grants when registry shows runtime had pre-approved snapshot (more complex). maybe avoid cached=true initially.

security-bot: Security note: make tokens single-use OR include nonce + jti store to prevent replay. Also include iat/nbf checks and require TLS for token transport.

ashley: Single-use requires issuing service to track jtis which is stateful at scale. Alternative: short TTL (2m) + nonce + artifact binding reduces replay risk sufficiently.

leo: performance ops: issuing many short lived tokens when traffic spikes could become a bottleneck. we should support a token-batch endpoint so agent can request N tokens with different nonces in one call.

maya: Good idea. Agent workflow: 1) request token-batch for X tokens bound to artifact-hash; 2) store tokens encrypted on host; 3) minted tokens consumed as needed. Add jittered refresh to avoid thundering herd.

ops: If a model is rolled back (artifact revoked), how do we revoke tokens already issued? we need a revocation list but that defeats stateless tokens.

security-bot: Revocation options: (A) Keep short TTL and accept delayed revocation; (B) use a revocation service consulted by runtime before every artifact fetch (adds latency); (C) include artifact revocation epoch in registry and require runtime to compare.

ashley: (C) sounds good: registry stores artifact_epoch; tokens issued after epoch X are valid only if runtime sees same epoch. For emergency revocations we bump epoch. Runtimes must check registry on connect or per X minutes.

leo: For network partitions, runtime should refuse to accept new tokens if it can't reach the registry AND the token's issued_at < now - grace_window. default: deny new artifact fetches (fail-closed) but allow cached inferences for up to 10m if artifact hash matches.

maya: Documented semantics:
- Artifact fetches: fail-closed without valid token or registry reachability.
- Cached inferences: allowed up to cached_ttl when registry unreachable, only if local artifact hash matches token binding.
- Telemetry/logging: buffer and ship later (fail-open).

ops: Agent details: it will run as a sidecar on customer runtime. responsibilities: rotate mTLS cert for controlplane callbacks, fetch token-batches, jittered refresh, local secure token store, leakproof file perms.

leo: Will agent accept unattended updates? we need an automatic upgrade path with rollout strategy in private environments. prefer canary then auto-upgrade with opt-out flag.

maya: Agreed. Also need an admission check: if agent binary missing or outdated, runtime should refuse hosted fallbacks (for security).

security-bot: Audit events: token_issue (issuer, jti, model_id, artifact_hash, ttl), token_use (jti, runtime_id, op_id), token_revoke, epoch_bump. retention: 90d default.

ashley: Ops issue created: RW-ops/2101 agent-sidecar-api and RW-ops/2102 artifact-epoch-revocation. infra-bot: tagging teams.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created RW-ops/2101, RW-ops/2102, assigned to ops and infra :white_check_mark:

maya: Next steps: security to draft token JSON schema and jitter rules; infra to prototype token-batch endpoint and light agent; ops to draft upgrade and admittance playbook. i'll sync with legal about retention.

leo: i'll sketch the registry fields and epoch bump flow.

ashley: i'll draft agent config sample and minimal file perms.

maya: ok thanks all — we'll take this into a short RFC (15m read). Post any concerns here. :thumbsup:
